title: ChatGPT and professional writing
script: Today I will present a replication of Noy and Zhang's study of generative AI and professional writing. I focus on the two main productivity outcomes: time spent and independently evaluated quality. I reconstruct the analysis samples, estimate the treatment effects, and compare them with the published benchmarks. I then report additional specification checks and an exploratory extension based on previous ChatGPT experience.
sources: Noy and Zhang (2023). Science 381(6654), 187–192. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adh2586. Author-hosted manuscript: https://shakkednoy.com/Noy%20Zhang%20NBER%20SI.pdf. Public data and code: https://osf.io/xd7qw/.

title: Research question and experimental design
script: The paper asks whether access to ChatGPT helps professionals complete writing tasks faster and produce better work. The experiment recruited 453 college-educated professionals in six occupations. Everyone completed two occupation-specific writing tasks. Between tasks, the researchers randomly assigned participants to register for ChatGPT or, in the control condition, Overleaf. Treated participants received guidance and could choose whether to use ChatGPT on the second task. The outcomes were self-reported time and blinded evaluations on a one-to-seven scale. About eighty percent of treated participants used ChatGPT, while some controls also used it. The treatment coefficient therefore estimates the effect of randomized encouragement. Interpreting it as the effect of actual use would require additional assumptions and an instrumental-variable analysis.
sources: Author-hosted manuscript, Method and Takeup of ChatGPT sections, pp. 3–4. https://shakkednoy.com/Noy%20Zhang%20NBER%20SI.pdf. Supplement A.1: https://shakkednoy.com/ChatGPT_SM.pdf.

title: Data, sample construction, and baseline summaries
script: The sample counts matter because the outcomes use different units of observation. Applying the cleaning rules gives 453 participants, of whom 359 belong to the linear and convex incentive arms used for the main productivity analysis. The remaining 94 belong to an exact-time arm. There are 356 recorded task-two time outcomes, but only 346 participants with both time measurements. The quality model uses one thousand participant-evaluator pairs from 352 people. The baseline summaries are broadly similar across assignment groups: time averages about twenty-nine to thirty minutes, and roughly one-third report previous ChatGPT use. These descriptive statistics use available observations for each variable. They should not be confused with the complete-case regression sample. Appendix two gives the missingness counts.
sources: scripts/clean.R, data/derived/analysis_sample.csv, and outputs/quality_sample.csv in the project. https://github.com/ZhanliangAaronWang/STAT5200-ChatGPT-Project. Authors' 2 - clean.do. Counts checked directly: 187 controls + 172 treated = 359; exact-time arm = 94. 356 is availability of time2, not the eligible main sample.

title: Empirical specification
script: For time, the dependent variable is task-two time minus task-one time. I regress this change on randomized treatment, occupation-by-task-order fixed effects, and incentive-arm fixed effects. The coefficient measures the adjusted difference in changes between assignment groups. A negative coefficient indicates larger time savings in treatment. I use HC1 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. For quality, the change is measured within each participant-evaluator pair. The model adds evaluator fixed effects because graders can differ systematically in their standards. Since several grades come from the same participant, I cluster standard errors by participant. I also standardize coefficients by the pretreatment outcome standard deviation using the authors' sample convention. Although the regression compares changes over time, its causal identification comes from randomized assignment. Attrition and missing outcomes can still affect the observed analysis sample.
sources: Supplementary Materials A.2, equations S.1 and S.2. https://shakkednoy.com/ChatGPT_SM.pdf. Authors' 4 - main text figures.do. Time uses HC1; quality uses CR1 with finite-sample correction and participant clusters. Confidence intervals use Student-t critical values with residual df or clusters minus one.

title: Replication result: time spent
script: The left panel uses exactly the 346 participants in the time regression. Control time falls from 28.97 to 26.88 minutes, while treated time falls from 29.68 to 16.83. The unadjusted difference in changes is minus 10.76 minutes. Adding the experimental design controls gives minus 10.84 minutes, with a robust standard error of 1.38. The confidence interval ranges from minus 13.56 to minus 8.12 minutes. The similarity of the unadjusted and adjusted estimates shows that the result is not driven by the included design controls. In standardized units, the adjusted estimate is minus 0.746, which rounds to minus 0.75, the value shown in the paper's Figure 1A. This reproduces the central time result.
sources: Own calculations from data/derived/analysis_sample.csv. outputs/time_verified.csv; replication/presentation_checks.py. Author-hosted manuscript, Figure 1A. Complete-case means differ slightly from variable-specific means shown in the original presentation; both tasks now use the same 346 observations.

title: Replication result: evaluated quality
script: The quality result points in the same direction as the time result: participants work faster and receive higher grades. In the paired observations, the control mean falls slightly, from 3.90 to 3.80, while the treatment mean increases from 3.95 to 4.52. The adjusted coefficient is 0.701 grade points, with a participant-clustered standard error of 0.154. Its confidence interval is approximately 0.398 to 1.005. Standardizing gives 0.411 standard deviations, with an interval from 0.233 to 0.590. This matches Figure 1B in the author-hosted manuscript. However, the prose reports 0.45 standard deviations. I retain this discrepancy explicitly rather than claiming the two benchmarks are identical. The chart is descriptive; the regression also accounts for evaluator and experimental design effects.
sources: Own calculations, outputs/quality_verified.csv and outputs/quality_sample.csv. Paired sample: 525 control rows and 475 treated rows. Author-hosted manuscript Figure 1B displays 0.41 SD and interval [0.23, 0.59], while Productivity prose reports 0.45 SD. https://shakkednoy.com/Noy%20Zhang%20NBER%20SI.pdf.

title: The changes extend beyond the group means
script: These empirical cumulative distributions provide another view of the outcomes. Each curve shows the fraction of observations at or below the value on the horizontal axis. For time, the treatment curve is generally higher: more treated participants finish within a given number of minutes. For quality, the treatment curve is lower over much of the grade scale: fewer treated submissions receive low grades. These descriptive patterns support the same directional interpretation as the regressions. They are not additional causal estimates or independent significance tests. The time plot uses participants; the quality plot uses the evaluator pairs used in the regression.
sources: Own empirical CDFs from the 346 complete time observations and 1,000 complete quality pairs. This is a descriptive reconstruction; the original Figure 1C–D uses density plots, not these ECDFs. Source code and data in the GitHub repository.

title: Specification and grader-screening checks
script: I then check how sensitive the conclusions are to selected modeling choices. For time, the unadjusted change regression, adjusted change regression, and ANCOVA all use the same 346 participants. ANCOVA models task-two time while controlling for task-one time and the experimental design variables. Its coefficient is minus 10.34 minutes, close to the main estimate of minus 10.84. For quality, I rerun the model while retaining the graders flagged by the authors' screening rule. The coefficient falls modestly from 0.701 to 0.655 grade points. The standardized effect changes from 0.411 to 0.386. These checks preserve the main directional conclusion. They do not resolve every threat to validity, particularly selection into the observed sample.
sources: Additional calculations in replication/presentation_checks.py and outputs/additional_results.csv. Main quality and retained-grader models use evaluator fixed effects and participant-clustered standard errors. ANCOVA is an additional specification check, not an exact reproduction of the paper's main change model.

title: Project extension: previous ChatGPT experience
script: My proposed extension asks whether previous users and nonusers benefit differently from the same randomized intervention. I add previous use and its interaction with treatment. The joint model estimates time savings of 12.27 minutes for previous nonusers and 8.00 minutes for previous users. The difference is positive 4.27 minutes, which would indicate smaller savings among previous users. However, its confidence interval runs from minus 1.47 to 10.01, and the p-value is 0.144. Thus, the estimates do not establish heterogeneity by experience at conventional significance levels. The standard error for previous users uses the covariance between the treatment and interaction coefficients. This analysis has 335 participants. Previous experience itself was not randomized, so the comparison does not identify the causal effect of acquiring experience.
sources: project/heterogeneity.R; replication/presentation_checks.py; outputs/additional_results.csv. Previous nonusers N = 226 (120 control, 106 treated); previous users N = 109 (53 control, 56 treated). Previous-user treatment effect is tau + delta, with its standard error calculated from the full covariance matrix. Exploratory analysis.

title: Conclusions and connection to the final project
script: The main replication result is that randomized encouragement reduces writing time by about eleven minutes and improves evaluated quality by about seven-tenths of a grade point. The standardized estimates match the two main figure coefficients to rounding, while the quality figure and prose remain inconsistent. The reconstruction also illustrates why sample definitions, evaluator effects, and clustering must be made explicit. There are important limits. Attrition differs between treatment and control, and these were short, incentivized tasks using an early version of ChatGPT. The results do not establish long-run employment or earnings effects. For the final project, I will investigate missingness by assignment and prior experience, then compare the self-reported time results with recorded task duration. The preliminary experience interaction remains inconclusive. The repository provides the data instructions, code, and numerical results.
sources: Author-hosted manuscript Method and Discussion; Supplement A.2–A.3. https://shakkednoy.com/ChatGPT_SM.pdf. Repository: https://github.com/ZhanliangAaronWang/STAT5200-ChatGPT-Project. Reported attrition: 6% control and 11% treatment.

title: Appendix: comparison with the reported benchmarks
script: This table separates original units from standardized units. Coefficients and their standard errors are divided by the available pretreatment standard deviation under the relevant outcome restrictions. The source code calculates this standard deviation outside the fitted model's complete-case restriction. The quality result matches the author-hosted Figure 1B, and the presentation does not claim to explain why that figure differs from the manuscript prose.
sources: Authors' 4 - main text figures.do. Source manuscript https://shakkednoy.com/Noy%20Zhang%20NBER%20SI.pdf. Replication outputs/productivity_summary.csv.

title: Appendix: sample and grading audit
script: The main eligible sample has 187 controls and 172 treated participants. Seven controls and six treated participants lack complete time changes. Seven controls and six treated participants lack previous-use responses. These are not identical sets, so the joint complete-case sample is 173 controls and 162 treated participants. Grader screening uses the authors' corrected July 2023 code and its pooled cross-grader regression slope threshold. Twenty-three of the 118 graders with eligible comparisons fall below 0.1. Keeping those graders provides the sensitivity analysis on slide eight.
sources: Own data audit; authors' 3 - grade cleaning_jul21.do and July 21 ReadMe at https://osf.io/xd7qw/. analysis_sample.csv, grader_screening.csv. Eligibility counts do not measure attrition from initial recruitment.

title: Appendix: specifications and references
script: The first equation is the additional ANCOVA check. The second shows how subgroup assignment effects follow from the interaction model. The final expression is the finite-sample-corrected clustered covariance estimator used for quality. Here M is the number of participant clusters, n is the number of grade-pair observations, and k is the rank of the design matrix. Confidence intervals use M minus one degrees of freedom for the quality model.
